title: Scriptorium Development Ledger

statusLegend.yellow: Present or claimed, but unaudited / unverified. Yellow is audit debt.
statusLegend.red: Not started, failed audit, known bad, blocked, or intentionally absent.

integratedDeliverable: A scholarly workspace for texts, locators, annotations, citations, threads, search, and cited retrieval output.
workflowRule: Move sequentially. One active gate at a time. Do not advance until the active gate is implemented, audited, CI-verified, and closed.

gates.title: Foundation / repo / architecture
gates.rationale: Base repository, app, schema, roadmap, and CI foundation.
gates.completionStandard: Repository has product docs, app skeleton, Prisma model, roadmap, and CI foundation.
evidence: README.md, ROADMAP.md, prisma/schema.prisma, and CI foundation exist.

gates.title: PDF scholarly workflow
gates.rationale: First complete proof of source metadata, page mapping, highlights, notes, citations, persistence, and reload.
gates.completionStandard: PDF scholarly workflow passes fixture, typecheck, build, and migration checks.

gates.title: TXT + Markdown scholarly ingestion
gates.rationale: Plain text and Markdown validate non-PDF text snapshots and locator rules before Office formats.
gates.completionStandard: TXT and Markdown upload, annotation, citation, persistence, and reload pass CI.

gates.title: Snapshot policy for text formats
gates.rationale: Text formats need durable versioned snapshots so annotations survive reimport.
gates.completionStandard: Snapshots are normalized, checksum-addressed, versioned, and verified.

gates.title: DOCX ingestion path
gates.rationale: DOCX support follows stable text snapshots because Office extraction has more failure modes.
gates.completionStandard: DOCX extracts readable text, snapshots it, supports annotation/citation, and passes CI.

gates.title: CSL source editor
gates.rationale: Citation metadata needs controlled editing before broader exchange workflows.
gates.completionStandard: CSL-compatible source records validate and persist.

gates.title: Citation import/export
gates.rationale: Scholarly source data needs bounded standard-format exchange.
gates.completionStandard: CSL JSON, BibTeX, and BibLaTeX exchange paths pass fixtures without source corruption.

gates.title: Zotero-compatible data path
gates.rationale: Local Zotero-shaped data compatibility follows stable citation exchange.
gates.completionStandard: Zotero-shaped book item data round-trips through Source.cslJson.

gates.title: Research threads
gates.rationale: Annotations become scholarship when grouped into ordered research trails.
gates.completionStandard: Threads persist ordered annotations, citations, source references, notes, and tags.

gates.title: Thread export
gates.rationale: Stable threads should render usable writing artifacts.
gates.completionStandard: Threads render to Markdown and RTF with order, notes, locators, citations, and source context preserved.

gates.title: Exact search
gates.rationale: Search begins with exact, inspectable, source-linked results.
gates.completionStandard: Documents, extracted passages, notes, tags, citations, and threads search with source and locator links.

gates.title: Semantic search
gates.rationale: Similarity retrieval must rest on trusted extracted passages and exact source linkage.
gates.completionStandard: Similarity results return source-linked passage records with stable locators.

gates.title: Grounded answer generation
gates.rationale: The final layer must use trusted retrieval.
gates.completionStandard: Outputs cite recovered source passages only.

gates.title: Expanded citation styles + richer CSL item types
gates.rationale: docs/CITATION_ENGINE.md names Turabian, APA, MLA, and Harvard as high-priority later styles, and the CSL editor only ever modeled plain books, which undercounts real theological citation (edited volumes, translated critical editions, journal articles). lib/citation-styles.ts adds all four styles alongside chicago-note/sbl-note; lib/citation-exchange.ts now models chapter/article-journal/manuscript with editor/translator/container-title/volume/edition and adds RIS export/import; a new additive route at /api/milestone-fourteen/csl-source-editor exposes the richer fields without touching the original, already-closed Milestone 6 route.
gates.completionStandard: All six styles produce distinct, locator-correct output for a real chapter/article fixture; BibTeX/BibLaTeX emit correct entry types (not everything forced into @book); RIS round-trips; Milestone 6's original route and its verifier remain unmodified and passing.
evidence: Pushed directly to main (commit 5203785; two follow-up fix commits 56222a4/cdbfd72 for an ES5-target regex issue and 25cba6c for an invalid Next.js route export, both surfaced by real CI, not opened as separate issues/PRs). Scriptorium CI #121, run 30228151197, commit 25cba6c: Typecheck and build + MySQL migration deploy both green.

gates.title: Citation regeneration
gates.rationale: ARCHITECTURE.md states generated citations are snapshots that should offer regeneration when source metadata or style changes, rather than silently changing old research notes — this was documented but never implemented; a corrected source name could leave stale footnotes with no way to detect or fix them. Added Citation.sourceSnapshotUpdatedAt (staleness baseline) and Citation.supersedesCitationId (regeneration lineage) via a hand-written MySQL migration, plus /api/milestone-fourteen/citation-regenerate (GET lists stale citations, POST regenerates by creating a new row that supersedes the old one and walks to the latest version in a chain rather than forking).
gates.completionStandard: Staleness is computed correctly against real timestamps; regeneration creates a new row rather than mutating the old one; a non-stale citation is not regenerated without an explicit override; regeneration reuses the shared citation-styles formatter rather than duplicating formatting logic.
evidence: Pushed directly to main (commit 5203785). Migration applied cleanly against real MySQL (prisma migrate deploy). Scriptorium CI #121, run 30228151197, commit 25cba6c: Typecheck and build + MySQL migration deploy both green.

gates.title: Corpus backup/export
gates.rationale: Scholarly data for a doctoral corpus is split across three stores — MySQL (annotations/citations/threads), local disk (PDF originals), and checksum-addressed text snapshots — with no single export covering all three, on a cPanel/shared-hosting deployment target where that matters more than on managed infrastructure. Added lib/server-storage.ts:listStoredFiles() (recursive on-disk file manifest) and /api/milestone-fifteen/corpus-export (full DB export: documents, versions, sources, page maps, text spans, annotations/tags, citations with regeneration lineage, and research threads, plus the storage manifest). QueryLog is intentionally excluded as telemetry, not scholarship.
gates.completionStandard: Export bundle plus a filesystem copy of SCRIPTORIUM_STORAGE_DIR together reconstruct the full corpus; storage manifest recursively covers nested snapshot directories with real file sizes and modification times.
evidence: Pushed directly to main (commit 5203785; the route's invalid Next.js export was caught by real CI and fixed in commit 25cba6c). Scriptorium CI #121, run 30228151197, commit 25cba6c: Typecheck and build + MySQL migration deploy both green.

gates.title: OCR pipeline contract for scanned PDFs
gates.rationale: FILE_INGESTION.md lists an OCR pipeline for scanned PDFs under 'Later' — high-priority in practice since older/rare theological sources are often page-image scans with no text layer, which currently defeats search, similarity, and text-anchored highlighting entirely and silently. Added lib/ocr-provider.ts (chars-per-page scan detection heuristic + a pluggable OcrProvider interface) and /api/milestone-sixteen/ocr-status (GET flags likely-scanned document versions; POST attempt fails loudly with a clear 501, not a silent no-op). Deliberately scoped as detection + hook only — no OCR engine is bundled or called.
gates.completionStandard: Detection heuristic correctly separates a real fixture with a healthy text layer from one with a near-empty one; the null provider throws a named, catchable error rather than returning empty text; nothing in the module quietly calls out to a real OCR engine or service.
evidence: Pushed directly to main (commit 5203785). Scriptorium CI #121, run 30228151197, commit 25cba6c: Typecheck and build + MySQL migration deploy both green. Note: a real OCR engine/service integration is still fully unbuilt and would be its own future gate — this gate covers detection + contract only, by design.

gates.title: Non-Latin script tokenization fix
gates.rationale: lib/local-similarity.ts's tokenizer split on /[^a-z0-9]+/ — ASCII only. Text in Greek, Ge'ez/Ethiopic, Syriac, Coptic, or other non-Latin scripts common in patristic and liturgical primary sources contains no characters matching that class, so it silently tokenized to an empty array: search and semantic-similarity scoring were completely blind to it, with no error or warning. Fixed to split on Unicode letter/number classes (\p{L}\p{N}) while keeping NFKD diacritic-stripping and English-specific stemming scoped only to ASCII tokens.
gates.completionStandard: Real Greek, Ge'ez, and Syriac sample text produce non-empty tokens and meaningful non-zero cosine similarity against overlapping excerpts of themselves; unrelated scripts still correctly score zero (no false positives); English tokenization/stemming output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
evidence: Pushed directly to main (commit 5203785; a regex compiled as an ES6+-only literal was caught by real CI and fixed via a RegExp-constructor workaround in commit cdbfd72). Scriptorium CI #121, run 30228151197, commit 25cba6c: Typecheck and build + MySQL migration deploy both green.

history.summary: Scriptorium was separated from Universal Office and defined as a scholarly reading platform.
Issue #1 and PR #2 closed the PDF scholarly workflow.
Issue #6 and PR #7 added TXT/Markdown ingestion.
Issue #8 and PR #9 added checksum-addressed snapshots.
Issue #10 and PR #11 added DOCX ingestion.
Issue #12 and PR #13 added CSL source editing.
Issue #14 and PR #15 added citation import/export.
Issue #16 and PR #17 added local Zotero-shaped compatibility.
Issue #18 and PR #19 added persistent research threads.
Issue #20 and PR #21 added Markdown and RTF thread rendering.
Issue #22 and PR #23 added bounded exact search with source and locator links.
Issue #24 and PR #25 added local deterministic source-linked similarity retrieval over trusted passages.
Issue #26 and PR #27 added cited output with passage evidence and unsupported-case refusal.
Commit 5203785 (plus fix commits 56222a4/cdbfd72/25cba6c) added Turabian/APA/MLA/Harvard styles and richer CSL item types; confirmed green by real CI run 30228151197.
Commit 5203785 added citation staleness tracking and regeneration lineage that creates new rows instead of mutating history; confirmed green by real CI run 30228151197.
Commit 5203785 added full corpus export plus an on-disk storage manifest; confirmed green by real CI run 30228151197.
Commit 5203785 added scanned-PDF detection and a pluggable OCR provider contract, deliberately without a bundled OCR engine; confirmed green by real CI run 30228151197.
Commit 5203785 fixed the ASCII-only search/similarity tokenizer to support Greek/Ge'ez/Syriac/Coptic and other non-Latin scripts; confirmed green by real CI run 30228151197.
